findings.claim: stop_reason() maps three documented Converse stopReason values — model_context_window_exceeded, malformed_model_output, malformed_tool_use — to StopReason.Complete, reporting a failed/truncated generation as a normally-completed turn.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED (doc + code + suite). AWS Converse API reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_Converse.html) stopReason Valid Values: 'end_turn | tool_use | max_tokens | stop_sequence | guardrail_intervened | content_filtered | malformed_model_output | malformed_tool_use | model_context_window_exceeded'. bedrock.baml:1080-1091 maps only tool_use/max_tokens/content_filtered/guardrail_intervened and falls through to '// end_turn, stop_sequence, and anything Bedrock adds later. -> Complete'. Suite test bedrock_parse_stop_reasons (crates/baml_tests/baml_src/ns_llm_bedrock/bedrock.baml:667-687) locks in 'something_new' -> Complete, so all three land on Complete today. model_context_window_exceeded means the prompt+output overflowed the window — the semantic twin of max_tokens — and malformed_* mean the model's output was unusable; an agent loop (require_done / terminal_text consumers) will treat the truncated or malformed turn as a clean final answer.
findings.suggested_fix: Map model_context_window_exceeded -> StopReason.MaxTokens; map malformed_model_output/malformed_tool_use to a non-Complete outcome (MaxTokens is wrong for them — likely throw ai.errors.ParseFailed with the raw stopReason, or Refused if throwing is too aggressive). Extend bedrock_parse_stop_reasons with the three values.

findings.claim: S3-sourced audio is hard-rejected ('Bedrock does not support S3 URIs for audio') based on a doc-comment claim that AudioSource has no s3Location member — but the current Converse API documents AudioSource as a union of bytes AND s3Location, so a documented capability is refused with a factually wrong message.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED (doc vs code). AudioSource reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_AudioSource.html): 'This data type is a UNION... bytes... s3Location: A reference to audio data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket.' AudioBlock reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_AudioBlock.html): 'The source of the audio data, which can be provided as raw bytes or an S3 location.' The implementation's AudioSource class (bedrock.baml:107-111) says 's3Location is not a member of AudioSource in the Converse API' and models bytes only; _audio_block (bedrock.baml:475-487) throws at :478-480 when the resolved media is not base64. sys_llm had the same rejection (crates/sys_llm/src/build_request/bedrock.rs:330-334) so this is parity-with-sys_llm, but it is not in the PLAN §6 deferral list and the stated API-shape justification is now false. Note ai.wire.resolve_media(audio, true) (bedrock.baml:476) inlines http(s) URLs, so the throw fires exactly for s3:// — the one URL scheme Bedrock actually accepts.
findings.suggested_fix: Add s3Location to the AudioSource class and route _media_source's s3 branch through it (delete the :478-480 throw), mirroring image/video/document; fix the :107-108 comment.

findings.claim: _prune_nulls recurses into replayed toolUse.input, silently deleting null-valued arguments the model itself authored — the exact 'user-authored JSON where a null is meaningful data' category the file's own opaque-key rationale (:303-309) protects for additionalModelRequestFields and inputSchema.json.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED empirically. Probe (scratchpad project, journal with AssistantMessage ToolUse args {"city":"SF","filter":null} + ToolCompleted): captured build_request body contains "toolUse":{"toolUseId":"tu_1","name":"get_weather","input":{"city":"SF"}} — "filter" is gone. _is_opaque_key (bedrock.baml:315-317) protects only 'additionalModelRequestFields' and 'json'; ToolUseBlock.input built at :639-646 is pruned like any wire object at build_request:968. The replayed conversation history therefore differs from what the model emitted; a tool schema with nullable parameters sees its explicit nulls vanish on every replay turn. (The native anthropic client's _anth_drop_nulls strips ALL nulls with no opaque keys at all — anthropic/ns_internal/messages.baml:159-185 — so this is a family-wide pattern; bedrock is strictly better but still lossy here, and unlike anthropic it already has the opaque-key machinery to fix it in one line.)
findings.suggested_fix: Treat 'input' under a toolUse block as opaque (either add a path-aware opaque check or mark the key 'input' opaque the way 'json' is), and extend bedrock_tool_replay with a null-valued arg.

findings.claim: An assistant-first conversation with no system content is sent as-is (messages[0].role == 'assistant'), unlike the sibling anthropic client which synthesizes a leading '(continue)' user turn because such a request 'is a guaranteed 400' — the same Claude model families run behind Bedrock Converse.
findings.evidence: PLAUSIBLE (wire shape CONFIRMED empirically; live rejection not run). Probe with prompt `${role("assistant")}carry on`: captured body is {"messages":[{"role":"assistant","content":[{"text":"carry on"}]}]} — no leading user message. converse_request (bedrock.baml:851-857) folds system into a leading user message only when system.length() > 0; there is no synthesize-user fallback for the system-empty case. Contrast anthropic/ns_internal/messages.baml:561-577: 'Assistant-first with NO system content: ... synthesize the leading user turn the API insists on. Without this the request is a guaranteed 400.' Claude models on Bedrock return ValidationException ('A conversation must start with a user message') for assistant-first message lists, so the same prompt that works through aws.BedrockClient's sibling AnthropicClient fails through BedrockClient with an InvalidRequest/400.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the anthropic client's synthesize_user branch: when messages is non-empty, first role != 'user', and system is empty, prepend a user message (e.g. '(continue)'). Also consider the messages.length() == 0 case (anthropic throws a local InvalidRequest; bedrock ships {"messages":[]}).

findings.claim: _lower_prompt merges every system message into the top-level system array, whereas PLAN §5's accepted multi-system decision says 'google: merge into systemInstruction; others: demote (2nd+ to user)'. Deviation from an accepted S5 row — though it matches the shipped anthropic native client, so it may be an unrecorded family-wide re-decision.
findings.evidence: bedrock.baml:585-607 pushes system blocks from EVERY role=='system' message into one system array (no demotion). _plan/sys_llm_native/PLAN.md:289 table row 'multi-system-message handling ... plan: google: merge into systemInstruction; others: demote (match engine UX)'. The anthropic native client does the same merge (anthropic/ns_internal/messages.baml:308-337), so either both deviate from the accepted decision or the decision text is stale — either way the plan and the implementations disagree and should be reconciled in writing.
findings.suggested_fix: Either demote 2nd+ system messages to user per the S5 row, or update PLAN §5 to record 'merge' as the shipped decision for anthropic-shaped providers (bedrock/anthropic).

findings.claim: toolResult.status ('success'/'error') is always sent, but the current docs say the field 'is only supported by Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude 3 and 4 models' — tool replay against other Bedrock families (Mistral, Llama, DeepSeek, ...) ships an unsupported field.
findings.evidence: UNVERIFIED live behavior (AWS may ignore rather than reject it), but the doc caveat is exact: ToolResultBlock reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_ToolResultBlock.html): 'status ... This field is only supported by Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude 3 and 4 models.' _push_tool_result (bedrock.baml:653-669) sets status unconditionally at :663-667. Since toolConfig support is net-new in this port (no sys_llm/engine precedent to inherit), the unconditional field is a fresh choice, not parity.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider emitting status only for the error case (the informative one), or documenting the model-family caveat on the client's tool options.

findings.claim: Local request-shaping rejections are split across two error identities: media/max_tokens problems throw baml.errors.InvalidArgument (which BedrockClient.invoke's normalize() wraps into an untyped baml.errors.UnknownError), while region/signing problems throw typed ai.errors.InvalidRequest — equally-local configuration errors surface to callers with different, partly untyped identities. Also the media format maps cover only a subset of the current documented enums (audio: 5 of 15 valid values — no opus/aac/m4a/mp4/mka/x-aac/mpga/pcm; video: no mpg/wmv mime mapping).
findings.evidence: _image_format/_video_format/_audio_format and the max_tokens range check throw baml.errors.InvalidArgument (bedrock.baml:372-375, :394-397, :412-415, :788-792); bedrock.baml root client invoke catch_all routes through ai.errors.normalize (aws/bedrock.baml:152-156), and normalize (ai/ns_errors/errors.baml:17-23) wraps non-Failure errors as UnknownError — while converse_url and sign throw typed ai.errors.InvalidRequest for the same class of pre-send config failure (bedrock.baml:896-914, :994-1007). Doc enums: AudioBlock format Valid Values 'mp3 | opus | wav | aac | flac | mp4 | ogg | mkv | mka | x-aac | m4a | mpeg | mpga | pcm | webm' (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_AudioBlock.html); VideoBlock 'mkv | mov | mp4 | webm | flv | mpeg | mpg | wmv | three_gp' (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_VideoBlock.html). The 5-format audio map is sys_llm parity (build_request/bedrock.rs:267-278) but the enum has since widened.
findings.suggested_fix: Throw ai.errors.InvalidRequest for media/max_tokens rejections (matching converse_url/sign), and extend the audio/video mime->format maps to the current enums.
